headline: A down week with a split inside it: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and chips 3.2% while small caps rose 2% and Brent jumped 6% to $116.72; next week's Fed meeting and big tech reports decide whether the AI sell off spreads.
summary: The dashboard has Friday Oct 23 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-23), so verdicts, zones and levels below are current to that close. For the week the S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,623.68, the Nasdaq 0.7% to 25,955.34 and the chip index 3.2%, while the Dow rose 0.4% and the Russell 2000 2.0% (AP, Yahoo Finance). The AI sell off reached the power and building names: GE Vernova fell 11.5% and Comfort Systems 19.3% for the week. Brent settled at $116.72, up 6% for the week, the 10 year ended at 4.99% and the VIX at 19.45. Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a warning, and Brazil votes Sunday with betting markets leaning to Flavio Bolsonaro. The scorecard has a data problem: by your own breakout rule none of its three finished swing grades would have been a trade. No swing, put or PMCC idea passes this week.

Breadth was weak on Friday (367 S&P 500 decliners against 135 gainers) and oil above $115 keeps a December Fed hike in play. With the Fed and three hyperscaler reports in four days, patience beats bargain hunting.

signals.title: Week in review: chips fell 3.2% and power stocks fell harder, with GE Vernova down 11.5% and Comfort Systems 19.3% for the week; Friday's chip bounce was small
signals.since_yesterday: Chips steadied on Friday (chip index up 0.4%), but power kept falling on heavy volume: Bloom Energy fell 11.2% and Comfort Systems 9.3% the day after their reports.
signals.what_happened: For the week to Oct 23 the S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,623.68, its second weekly loss, the Nasdaq fell 0.7% to 25,955.34, the Dow rose 0.4% to 52,215.16 and the Russell 2000 rose 2.0% to 2,775.90 (AP). The Philadelphia chip index rose 0.4% Friday to 10,779.46 but fell 3.2% for the week from 11,137.29 (Yahoo Finance). Weekly moves from Oct 16 to Oct 23 closes (Yahoo Finance): LRCX down 12.8% to 230.10, META down 9.4% to 642.62, NVDA down 1.5% to 210.96, MSFT down 0.9% to 524.51. Power and AI building names fell more: GEV down 11.5% to 815.00, FIX down 19.3% to 1,160.86, BE down 12.7% to 193.30, VST down 7.8%, CEG down 6.6%, ETN down 6.4%, VRT down 5.9%. On Friday alone BE fell 11.2% on 2.36 times normal volume and FIX 9.3% on 3.46 times (dashboard), despite strong reports on Oct 22. Breadth was weak Friday: 135 S&P 500 stocks rose and 367 fell (Dean Financials). Reuters says third quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to rise more than 32% from a year ago (LSEG), and hyperscaler spending is expected to be about $800 billion this year.
signals.so_what: The sell off walked down the money trail this week: first the big buyer (Meta, on its spending and credit), then the chip tool makers (Lam), then the power and building contractors who get paid last. Profits are not the problem; the market is asking who pays for next year's build and with what. When a company posts a record backlog and still falls 19% in a week, as Comfort Systems did, investors are discounting that backlog, not doubting it exists. What would make this wrong: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon raising 2027 spending next week while showing cash flow that covers it. That is the test for every name on this list.
signals.for_you: Swing: none. No AI or power name is a setup, and most are falling on heavy volume. Long term: NVDA (210.96, zone 197.26 to 229.06) and MRVL (228.51, zone 218.04 to 250.20) stay 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'; GEV is Wait at 815.00, below its 910.20 zone bottom, and reports Oct 28. MSFT is 'Buy zone now' at 524.51 but reports Oct 28: wait for the report. Puts: none on AI or power names with a report inside the expiry.

signals.title: Brent rose 6% for the week to $116.72, its highest close since April 29, and energy led Friday's market; the 10 year ended the week at 4.99%
signals.since_yesterday: Brent rose another 3.14% on Friday after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and a tanker spill off the UAE, and the US lent reserve oil to a Phillips 66 refinery.
signals.what_happened: Brent settled at $116.72 on Oct 23, up $3.55 or 3.14%, its highest close since April 29 and up 6% for the week; WTI rose 3.8% to $103.27 and 2.3% for the week (Reuters via Nation Thailand). AP called Brent's level the highest since June 2022; sources disagree on the comparison, and the close is the same. The drivers were Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, an Aramco order on Oct 22 for staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters, and an oil spill from a tanker off the UAE. The Energy Department approved an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels from the strategic reserve, now at its lowest since 1982, for a disruption at Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery. Energy was the best sector Friday, up 2.6% (Dean Financials): SLB rose 7.1% to 53.06 and HAL 5.2% to 34.92 (dashboard), CVX 2.9% and COP 3.6% (AP). Dollar General and Dollar Tree fell more than 5% after Wells Fargo warned diesel costs would squeeze profits, and UAL fell 4.0% to 97.93 (CNBC, dashboard). The 10 year yield ended at 4.99%, up from 4.96% Thursday (AP) and down from about 5.10% a week earlier (Yahoo Finance). Futures put the chance of a Fed hike on Oct 28 at 5% and of a December hike at about 80% (LSEG via Reuters, Oct 22).
signals.so_what: Who pays: anyone who burns diesel and jet fuel, from discount stores to airlines, and in the end the consumer. Who gets paid: US producers and oil service firms, whose Middle East work is growing. The strategic reserve is the US's shock absorber, and it is at a 44 year low, which leaves less room to cap prices if a big supply loss comes. The bond market's message changed during the week: yields fell below 5% on growth fears, then held near 5% as oil kept rising, which keeps a December Fed hike in play. What would make this wrong: a real ceasefire, which could take $10 or more off Brent fast.
signals.for_you: Swing: if you hold the dashboard's energy swings, all are in profit on Oct 23 closes and buyers lead: XOM 183.21 (stop 162.99, up/down 1.55), CVX 233.21 (stop 210.45, 1.19), COP 150.80 (stop 135.75, 1.13), EOG 163.03 (stop 147.98, 1.43). XOM and CVX report Oct 30: no new energy swings into that date. PSX is 283.18, below its 292.08 entry (stop 275.15), and its Lake Charles plant has a supply problem: watch it. HAL moved to 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' at 34.92 (zone 34.44 to 35.15) but sellers still lead (0.94). Airlines: UAL stays Avoid, DAL 'wait for the chart' at 76.78. Puts: the 4.99% 10 year is the bar a put premium must beat.

signals.title: Moody's kept France at Aa3, a reprieve with a warning; the Nov 3 budget vote is the next test
signals.since_yesterday: The decision came after Friday's close: no downgrade, outlook still negative.
signals.what_happened: Moody's kept France's Aa3 rating with a negative outlook on Oct 23, sparing it the cut to A1 that most analysts expected (AFP via Euronext, Bloomberg). It said the review was not a rating action, warned that more evidence of weaker capacity in parliament to prevent a steep and lasting rise in debt costs would likely lead to a downgrade, and said its view assumes a 2027 budget is approved. S&P (May 29) and Fitch (Aug 28) already rate France A+. The National Assembly's revenue vote on the 2027 budget is set for Nov 3. French bond yields eased a little on Friday and the CAC 40 fell 0.4% (AP); the French 10 year was 5.07% on Oct 22 (AFP).
signals.so_what: A cut was mostly priced in, so the hold is mild relief rather than a turn. The risk has moved to the calendar: the Nov 3 budget vote lands the same day as the US midterms, and the ECB decides on Oct 29 with euro area inflation at 3.2%. Second order: if France stabilizes, it removes one reason for global bond yields to rise, which helps the US 10 year stay under 5%.
signals.for_you: No action. No dashboard name is French. European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) are a wait until the Nov 3 vote; they are left out of both lists because the relief and the warning cut both ways.

signals.title: Brazil votes Sunday: the polls are close to a tie, betting markets favor Flavio Bolsonaro, and Brazilian prices lean the same way
signals.since_yesterday: The Ibovespa rose 0.47% Friday and the real moved back below 5 per dollar; Polymarket priced Flavio Bolsonaro at 76.9%.
signals.what_happened: The runoff between President Lula and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro is Sunday Oct 25; the electoral court starts publishing the count at 4pm ET. Flavio won the first round 47.03% to 45.16%. Final polls: Datafolha 50% to 50% of valid votes (Oct 22), AtlasIntel/Bloomberg 51.1% to 48.9% for Flavio (Oct 19, one point margin), and the Rio Times average of 41 polls about 51% to 49% for Flavio, who leads in 35 of them. Polymarket priced Flavio at 76.9% (Oct 23, 7:24pm ET). On Oct 23 the Ibovespa rose 0.47% to 205,082.56 (down 0.17% for the week, up 10.06% in October) and the real strengthened about 0.9% to 4.993 per dollar (Agencia Brasil via Rio Times). EWZ closed at 42.59, up 1.8% on 2.27 times normal volume and up 15.4% in a month (dashboard); it jumped 12.54% on Oct 5 after the first round (Rio Times). Brazil's finance minister called Flavio's $39.7 billion spending cut plan impossible (Oct 23), and an extra 25% US tariff still covers most Brazilian goods.
signals.so_what: Markets have already moved toward a Flavio win, so the two results are not equal in size. If Flavio wins: much of the gain is in the price; expect a modest move, and the next question is whether his spending cuts can pass, which matters for Brazil's rates and the real. If Lula wins: it is the surprise against about 77% betting odds, and the October rally could reverse quickly; the usual first hit is the real, then banks (ITUB, NU) and Petrobras (PBR), where investors fear more state control of fuel prices. MELI earns in several countries, so it is hit through the currency more than through policy. This is a read of how markets are positioned, not a forecast.
signals.for_you: No Brazil trades before Monday's open. NU is 'Buy zone now' at 15.16, just above its 14.13 to 15.02 zone, and reports Nov 12: if Lula wins and NU falls into the zone, wait for the selling to stop before a small first buy; if Flavio wins, do not chase a gap up. EWZ, ITUB and PBR have no verdict; all three are in uptrends (PBR up 49.6% in 3 months). MELI is rated Avoid. If you sold the Setups scanner's EWZ $37 put for Nov 20 (Oct 12), it has a 15.1% cushion. No name goes in either list: the result is a coin flip in the polls.

signals.title: Scorecard: how the calls did
signals.what_happened: From site/data/scorecard.json (calls since Oct 6, graded Oct 24 on Oct 23 closes). Swing: 20 calls, 3 finished: 1 win (ABBV +2R) and 2 losses (ZBRA and ANET, -1R each), average 0.0R; 13 open, 4 waiting. Open swings in profit: CVX +1.93R, XOM +1.89R, COP +1.44R, EOG +1.32R, BDX +0.86R, PFE +0.70R, WST +0.47R, GILD +0.22R; below entry: MET -0.59R, PSX -0.53R, AMGN -0.42R, MSFT -0.37R, ZBRA -0.27R. Puts: 10 open, none expired yet (all Nov 20); BHP $82.50 is 5.6% in the money, and C $120 (0.5% cushion) and IBKR $80 (0.3%) are at their strikes; the brief's PFE $27 has 11.2% and JPM $310 7.0%. Long term buys: 46 of 103 graded calls beat the S&P 500 over 5 days (45%), 2.76 points behind on average. By group (my grouping of tickers): health care 18 of 20 beat it (3.28 points ahead), AI chips and power 2 of 23 (9.05 behind). Signals: right in 58 of 95 graded calls (61%), 1.13 points ahead on average. By the same grouping, bullish energy 9 of 9 and bullish health 13 of 13; bullish AI chip and power 2 of 13 (6.97 behind); bearish AI hardware 8 of 8; bearish energy 0 of 5 and bearish health 0 of 5. Data problem: the scorecard counts a swing as triggered when the day's high touches the entry. Your rule needs a close over the pivot on at least 1.5 times normal volume. Checking every triggered swing against Yahoo Finance daily bars (volume against the prior 50 day average), only EOG met that rule on its trigger day (Oct 16, close 158.01 on 1.77 times). All three finished grades are affected: ZBRA (Oct 7 high 387.51 but close 386.05, under its 387.01 entry, on 0.69 times volume), ANET (close 215.83 just over 215.33 on 0.82 times) and ABBV (close 272.42 on 1.17 times; its first close over the entry on 1.5 times volume came Oct 15, the day it hit its target). The same applies to AMGN (Oct 22 close 447.28 under 447.93, 1.11 times) and ZBRA's second call (Oct 21 close 391.00 under 391.59, 0.55 times), which the scorecard shows as open.
signals.so_what: What works: following the money into energy and health care while it is moving there, and bearish calls on AI hardware. What does not: bullish calls and long term buys in AI chips and power, which lost to the S&P 500 for a second straight week, and bearish calls that fight a sector the money is flowing into. The honest caveat is bigger than usual: by your own breakout rule, the swing record has zero finished trades, because none of the three closed calls would have been entered. Every group has fewer than 20 finished calls, and three weeks of one unusual market is not proof of anything.
signals.for_you: Rule change to consider: grade a swing as triggered only on a close over the entry on at least 1.5 times normal volume, and count the rest as 'never confirmed'. That makes the scorecard test the rule you actually trade. Until the code changes, read the swing hit rate as a test of a looser rule. If you hold the AMGN or second ZBRA swings, by your rule they have not triggered: AMGN needs a close over 447.93 on about 4.2 million shares, ZBRA over 391.59 on about 818,000 shares (1.5 times their 50 day averages, my calculation). If you sold the scanner's BHP, C or IBKR puts, decide before Nov 20 whether you would take the shares; none is 'Buy zone now', so do not roll them.

signals.title: Week ahead: the Fed on Wednesday, then Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Intel and SK hynix test the AI spending story; Apple waits until Nov 2
signals.what_happened: Verified dates (Eastern time): SK hynix releases Q3 before 9am Seoul time on Oct 28, which is 8pm ET Tuesday Oct 27, with its call at 9am Seoul (company invitation). The Fed meets Oct 27 to 28 and decides at 2pm ET Wednesday, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference; futures show about a 5% chance of a hike and about 80% for December (LSEG via Reuters). Alphabet and Microsoft report after the close Oct 28 (calls 4:30pm and 5:30pm ET per StockTitan). Amazon reports after the close Oct 29 (call 5pm ET), and Intel and Sandisk also report this week (Reuters). September PCE inflation comes Oct 29 at 8:30am ET (BEA), with AP citing an expected 3.7% rate. ExxonMobil reports Oct 30 (release 6:30am ET, call 9:30am ET) and Chevron holds its call Oct 30 at 11am ET. Meta already reported on Oct 21. Samsung's full Q3 date is not confirmed: trackers estimate Oct 29, after preliminary results on Oct 8 of about 195 trillion won in sales and 107.4 trillion won in operating profit. Apple reports Nov 2 after the close, not this week. About a third of S&P 500 companies report (Reuters).
signals.so_what: This is the week the market gets its answer to the question it sold on: is AI spending paid for with cash or with debt? Three hyperscalers worth a combined $10.5 trillion report within two days (Opening Bell Daily). If they raise 2027 spending and show the cash to cover it, chips and power can bounce from oversold levels; if they slow spending or lean on debt, the sell off likely spreads further down the chain. SK hynix and Samsung are the read on memory prices. The Fed is not expected to move, so the market will trade Warsh's words about December and Thursday's PCE.
signals.for_you: No new positions in names reporting this week: MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, INTC, GEV (Oct 28 before the open), LLY, DXCM, XOM, CVX, and the 'Buy zone now' names PYPL (Oct 27) and BLCO (Oct 28). If you hold swings, expect bigger gaps around Wednesday and Thursday. For puts, pick expiries that end before a report or skip the name.

cycle.quadrant: Inflation rising, growth starting to wobble
cycle.quadrant_why: Inflation: September PCE is expected near 3.7% (AP) and Brent closed at $116.72 on Oct 23, up 6% in a week. Growth: Q2 GDP grew at a 2.2% rate, down from 2.5% in Q1 (BEA third estimate), and bond yields fell below 5% midweek on slowdown fears before ending at 4.99%. Profits are still strong (Q3 S&P 500 earnings on pace for more than 32% growth, LSEG via Reuters).
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Late. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023 and is expected to hold on Oct 28, with futures near 80% for a December hike (LSEG via Reuters). Credit costs are rising at the top of the AI build: Meta's credit default swap hit a record on Oct 22, and a strategist cited by Reuters says the market is no longer giving big spenders the benefit of the doubt.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. France kept its Moody's Aa3 rating only with a warning, its 10 year near 5%, and the US strategic oil reserve is at its lowest since 1982, which leaves governments less room to absorb the next shock.
cycle.big_cycle: Four of five forces are active. External order: Houthi attacks inside Saudi Arabia and a war with Iran that Trump says could end quickly or wind down slowly. Internal order: the Nov 3 US midterms, Brazil's runoff and French unrest. Debt and money: sovereign yields near 5% and AI builders funding with debt and leases. Technology: the AI build is still growing, but the market is repricing who pays for it.
tailwinds: Q3 S&P 500 earnings are on pace to grow more than 32% (LSEG via Reuters).
Small caps rose 2.0% for the week while large caps fell, so money is rotating, not leaving.
Moody's spared France a downgrade, easing one source of bond market stress.
headwinds: Brent at $116.72, up 6% in a week, with the US reserve at a 44 year low.
AI power and building names fell 6% to 19% for the week on heavy volume.
A December Fed hike is about 80% priced, and PCE on Oct 29 could raise it.

history.when: Summer and fall 1990, the Gulf War oil shock
history.what: After Iraq invaded Kuwait, oil rose from $17 a barrel in July to $36 in October 1990, peaked near $46 in mid October, then fell steadily until 1994.
history.lesson: War premiums in oil can double prices quickly, but they fade once supply proves it can keep flowing. Kpler showed Hormuz flows near prewar levels on Oct 22 while Brent kept rising, which looks like a premium on fear of the next strike.

history.when: 2000 to 2002, the dot com and telecom build out
history.what: The Nasdaq fell from 5,048.62 on March 10, 2000 to 1,114.11 on Oct 9, 2002, about 78%. Internet use kept growing, but builders had funded capacity with debt and new stock, and suppliers were hit hardest.
history.lesson: This week the selling reached the last link in the chain, the contractors and power gear makers, even as their orders hit records. That is how a funding scare spreads; it is not yet proof of a top.

cycle.differences: The 2008 oil spike comparison is swapped for 1990 because the story this week is a war premium on supply fears, not demand collapsing. What is different from 1990: the US is now a large oil producer, so high prices help part of its economy. What is different from 2000: the biggest AI buyers still earn huge profits, and the power shortage is physical.
